observations: Two large white-outlined oval forms sit side by side near the top center, each filled with dense black scribble lines, set against a teal background with blue, pink, and brown color blocks behind them.
Below the oval forms, a wide rectangular zone is packed with dense vertical black lines on white, enclosed by a loose white outline and flanked by orange-brown and blue strokes on either side.

A horizontal tangle of white, black, and yellow lines crosses the very top of the image beyond the central form, while a separate white rectangular shape with yellow and black marks sits to the right of the main structure.
reading: Two dark-filled oval forms anchor the upper half; their interiors are dense scribble rather than clear pupils. Below them, vertical black lines packed into a white rectangle give the lower section a grid-like, mechanical quality. The teal field holds the layered color blocks—pink, brown, blue, yellow—apart from one another. The overall effect reads as blunt and slightly unsettled.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, #75 sits between title neighbors #74 and #76. Where #74 fills its field with deep warm reds and a single large dark void, #75 switches to a cool teal ground with a busier multi-color scaffold—a strong tonal contrast across adjacent titles.

connections.reason: Both #75 and #76 share a teal background, paired rectangular eye zones, and vertical-line grids in the lower section, making them the clearest structural pair among the inspected owned neighbors.
nnotb #98 shares the same flat teal ground as #75, and both works place dark, mark-filled forms against that field—the visual quality the collector links to scrimshaw's dark marks on a light surface.

lookingQuestion: What happens to your reading of the two oval forms when you follow the dense scribble lines inside them—do they hold as eyes, or does the interior mark-making pull them toward something else?
ambiguities: The white rectangular shape to the right of the main form has an unclear spatial relationship to the central structure—whether it is attached or a separate floating element is not resolvable from the image alone.

Title-derived order and recorded-creation order align for this work, but gaps exist elsewhere in the owned subset, so adjacency to #74 and #76 is a title relationship, not a confirmed making sequence.
